answer_text:
A complex-valued function does not have a natural “maximum” unless we mean the maximum of its modulus. Interpreting the question in the standard way, we maximize

\[
|f(z)|=\left|\frac{1}{z-\frac i2}\right|=\frac{1}{\left|z-\frac i2\right|}.
\]

Thus we need to minimize the distance \(\left|z-\frac i2\right|\) over the annulus

\[
1\le |z|\le 2.
\]

By the reverse triangle inequality,

\[
\left|z-\frac i2\right|
\ge \bigl||z|-\left|\frac i2\right|\bigr|
= \left||z|-\frac12\right|.
\]

Since \(|z|\ge 1\),

\[
\left||z|-\frac12\right|
= |z|-\frac12
\ge 1-\frac12
= \frac12.
\]

So

\[
\left|z-\frac i2\right|\ge \frac12,
\]

which gives

\[
|f(z)|\le \frac{1}{1/2}=2.
\]

Equality occurs when \(|z|=1\) and \(z\) lies in the same direction as \(\frac i2\), namely

\[
z=i.
\]

Indeed,

\[
f(i)=\frac{1}{i-\frac i2}=\frac{1}{\frac i2}=-2i,
\]

so \(|f(i)|=2\).

Therefore the maximum value of \(|f(z)|\) on the set is

\[
\boxed{2}.
\]
